clue.text: Expenses for constructing emu's bird's-nest

indicators.note: constructing means building something new out of these letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter here
the S of the possessive is kept as a letter here, and the hyphen is ignored

explanation.surface: Someone totting up the cost of building a nest for an emu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructing' rearranges all thirteen letters of EMUS BIRDSNEST; 'for' only links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbursements are payments made out of a fund, so they are outgoings or costs.

clue.text: Final result the match is over

definitions.text: Final result the match is over

parts.words: Final result the match is over
parts.note: reads like a sports result, but the match is a marriage and the final result is the court order ending it

explanation.walkthrough: In English divorce law the decree nisi was followed by the order that finally dissolved the marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: This court order is the last step of a divorce, the moment a marriage legally ends.

clue.text: Peak of tablet dispensary according to the book

definitions.text: Peak of tablet dispensary according to the book

parts.words: Peak of tablet dispensary according to the book
parts.note: the tablets are not pills but the stone tablets of the Commandments, handed out on a mountain according to the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensary' suggests a pharmacy; the book is the Bible, where Moses received the tablets of the law on this mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Exodus, Moses receives the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments on this mountain.

clue.text: Flat out from uneven deal

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are flatly out of a lopsided deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges UNEVEN DEAL; 'from' is a link. 'Flat' describes bread made without yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread baked without yeast or raising agent does not rise, so it stays flat.

clue.text: Witnessed invoice for merganser

parts.note: to have witnessed something is to have seen it
an invoice is a bill for goods or work

explanation.surface: A bill for a duck, signed by a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: The sawbill is another name for the merganser, a fish-eating duck with a serrated beak.

clue.text: Utmost degree to cross single mother

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
a cross is the letter X
single means one, the Roman numeral I
mum is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A single mother is pushed to the utmost to cross some boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utmost degree' looks like one phrase, but 'degree' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest possible amount or extent is the utmost.

clue.text: Knows how to pronounce scent

indicators.note: says the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: taken as written, then said out loud

explanation.surface: A perfumer is an expert in saying the names of scents.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet or smell is called its nose.

clue.text: First class return to Avon to see the star

parts.note: super means excellent, first-rate

indicators.note: return means go back, so the word Avon is read backwards

parts.note: the English river, taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-class trip back to the River Avon to see a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the river's name backwards; 'to see the' links the wordplay to the definition. 'First class' looks like travel but means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is an exploding star that briefly outshines its galaxy.

clue.text: A flag designer who's work is looked down on

definitions.text: A flag designer who's work is looked down on

parts.words: A flag designer who's work is looked down on
parts.note: the flag is a paving flagstone, and the work is literally looked down on by passers-by, not despised

explanation.walkthrough: 'flag designer' suggests banners and 'looked down on' scorn; this street artist chalks pictures on the paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A street artist who chalks pictures on paving stones draws work that pedestrians look down at.

clue.text: It may offer light relief from a wicked heart

definitions.text: It may offer light relief from a wicked heart

parts.words: It may offer light relief from a wicked heart
parts.note: the heart is wicked because it holds a wick, and the substance round it gives light

explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' means having a wick, and 'light relief' is literal: the material burns round the wick to give light.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuel of a candle is the wax that surrounds the wick and burns to give light.

clue.text: The sea has a good colour

indicators.note: has means holds, so the sea holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: taken as written
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: The sea is a pleasant colour today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' puts PI inside SEA; 'The' and 'a' are links. PI for good (pious) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown shade, named after the cuttlefish ink once used for it.

clue.text: Heather seen by the heath?

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, so another girl's name answers it
a plant found growing on heathland, the botanical genus of heaths

explanation.walkthrough: Both Heather and this answer are girls' names, and the answer is also the Latin genus of heath plants.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name like Heather, and also the scientific genus of heathers growing on moorland.

clue.text: Am I first to finally stub a foot

indicators.note: first says the letter I is put at the front of the words Am I
finally takes the last letter of the word stub

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they will be first to stub a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' moves I to the front of AM I, giving I AM; 'finally' takes B, the end of 'stub'. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry a foot is a unit of rhythm, and this one is a short syllable followed by a long one.

clue.text: Release engineer in iron jacket

indicators.note: a jacket wraps round something, so the iron symbol is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RE, the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineers

explanation.surface: An engineer is freed from an iron jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' puts RE inside FE; 'in' is a link. RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone at liberty is to release them.

clue.text: Afraid of dirt so follow my irrational fears

indicators.note: follow says the word so comes after the word my

parts.note: taken as written
phobic means having phobias, irrational fears

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow their own irrational fears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' sets the small word 'so' after 'my'; 'irrational fears' stands for the adjective describing someone who has phobias.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysophobia is a morbid fear of dirt or contamination, from the Greek for filth.

clue.text: Ambition of thespian to perform with decorum

definitions.meaning: what any actor hopes to do on stage: give a good performance
to behave properly, as a matter of conduct

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is acting skilfully on stage; the other is behaving well in everyday life.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor hopes to perform skilfully, and anyone may be urged to behave properly; the phrase covers both.

clue.text: Strap up American saloon with pastes

parts.note: to tape something is to strap or bind it

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the saloon word is reversed

parts.note: a sedan is the American name for a saloon car

explanation.surface: Someone straps up an American saloon bar along with some pastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the car word backwards, as suits a down clue; 'with' is a link. 'saloon' suggests a bar but means a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapenade is a Provençal spread of olives, capers and anchovies, so these are savoury pastes.

clue.text: Might European be held by dancers

definitions.note: a description of the object: something to be held by dancers

parts.note: may and might both express possibility
a Pole is a person from Poland, a European

explanation.surface: Could a European be held aloft by a troupe of dancers?
explanation.walkthrough: Dancers round this tall decorated post each hold a ribbon tied to its top.
explanation.definitionFit: On May Day, dancers circle a tall post, each holding a ribbon fixed to its top.

clue.text: Drink leads regiment to get the highest

indicators.note: leads says the drink word goes in front of the regiment word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Drink spurs a regiment on to win the top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' looks like the first letters of 'regiment', but it puts SUP ahead of REME. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means greatest in rank or degree, at the very top.

clue.text: Promised, and hoped the match would not get one down

definitions.text: hoped the match would not get one down
definitions.meaning: a betrothed couple hopes the coming match, their marriage, will not depress them

explanation.walkthrough: The match is a marriage, which an affianced pair hopes will not get them down.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple pledged to marry are betrothed, looking forward to their wedding.

clue.text: It's read as a warning from Brazilian port to adopt diplomacy

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major port in Brazil
tact is skill in handling people diplomatically

explanation.surface: A warning from Rio urging the city to be more diplomatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'to adopt' are links. The 1714 Riot Act was read aloud to disperse crowds, so to read it now means to give a stern warning.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British law ordering crowds to disperse was read out to them, hence a severe reprimand.

clue.text: Wait after notebook

indicators.note: after says the waiting word comes after the note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: Someone told to wait until they have finished with their notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notebook' splits into 'note' (a sol-fa note) and 'book' (the definition), with 'after' putting the waiting word behind the note.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance.

clue.text: On borrowed time so close to Easter

definitions.meaning: loaned out, the other side of borrowing
the forty days of fasting in the church year just before Easter

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is loaned; the other is the Christian season of fasting leading up to Easter. 'On' and 'so' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Money given on loan has been loaned out, and the Christian season of fasting falls just before Easter.

clue.text: Turkish leaders reads of an entertaining situation

definitions.meaning: aghas or ... were Ottoman military commanders and chiefs
a gas is a slang term for something great fun

explanation.walkthrough: The plural title of Ottoman chiefs also reads as A GAS, slang for a lot of fun. 'reads of' joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghas were Ottoman officials, and 'a gas' is slang for an enjoyable time.

clue.text: Linger how to begin before being finished

indicators.note: before places that letter ahead of the finished word
to begin takes only the first letter of the word how

parts.note: over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, wondering how to begin before the task is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to begin' gives H, the start of 'how'; 'before' places it ahead of OVER. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to hang about in one place, waiting.

clue.text: Big flower gives heart to miss korbut

indicators.note: heart takes the centre letter of the word gives

parts.note: Olga Korbut is the Soviet gymnast who starred at the 1972 Olympics

explanation.surface: A big bouquet of flowers lifts the spirits of gymnast Olga Korbut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means something that flows, a river. 'heart' gives V, the middle of 'gives'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a thing that flows, and this is Europe's longest, running through Russia.

clue.text: It could raise the body temperature quite a bit

definitions.text: It could raise the body temperature quite a bit

parts.words: It could raise the body temperature quite a bit
parts.note: sounds like a fever, but the body is a corpse placed on a fire for cremation

explanation.walkthrough: 'body temperature' suggests a fever; the body is a corpse being burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of wood on which a corpse is burnt at a funeral heats the body greatly.

clue.text: Trifle with theologian having hot drink

indicators.note: with here means holding inside, so the trifle word carries the theologian within it

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian trifles with a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' puts the divinity degree inside the plaything word; 'having' is a link. 'Trifle' suggests the dessert but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: Biscuit that conquered Sicily and Naples

definitions.meaning: a currant-filled biscuit, popular in Britain
the Italian general who led the Thousand in 1860

explanation.walkthrough: A Garibaldi is a British biscuit with squashed currants, nicknamed 'squashed fly', named after the Italian hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The currant biscuit is named after the Italian patriot whose Redshirts took Sicily and Naples in 1860.

clue.text: A hasty drug dealer?

parts.note: read literally, a trader in the drug amphetamine, but the phrase means someone who drives fast

explanation.walkthrough: SPEED is slang for amphetamine and a merchant is a dealer, but the phrase means a fast driver or runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who loves going fast, especially a reckless driver, is called this.
